name: CEPF Guinean Forests of West Africa Biodiversity Hotspot grants
summary: CEPF small and large grants for civil society groups conserving forest biodiversity in the Guinean Forests of West Africa hotspot, from Guinea to Cameroon, with A Rocha Ghana and AJESH as the regional implementation team.
reporting: Large-grant holders file financial reports every quarter and progress reports every six months through CEPF’s online system.

steps: Letter of inquiry (small or large grant)

eligibility.rule: Project supports at least one strategic direction in the hotspot ecosystem profile
Has its own bank account and is legally authorized to receive grants
If government-owned: independent legal personality, can receive private funds, no sovereign immunity
No child or forced labor, large or complex dams, government security salaries, firearms or other weapons
Project does not physically resettle people or purchase land
Project does not introduce or use potentially invasive, non-indigenous species
Project does not remove or alter tangible cultural heritage
No critical-habitat harm unless limited conservation impacts yield net biodiversity gain

calls.label: Call for letters of inquiry, small grants (July 2026)

status.quote: Guinean Forests of West Africa Call for Letters of Inquiry for Small Grants Closed Monday, 31 August, 2026.

deadline.quote: no later than 31 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. GMT/UTC

calls.label: First call for letters of inquiry, large grants (March 2026)

status.quote: Guinean Forests of West Africa First Call for Letters of Inquiry for Large Grants Closed Monday, May 11, 2026.

administered_by.quote: A Rocha Ghana and AJESH, serving as the Regional Implementation Team for the Guinean Forests of West Africa Biodiversity Hotspot on behalf of the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)

applicant_types.quote: small grants from non-governmental organizations, community groups, private enterprises, independent public institutions and other civil society organizations (CSOs)

geography.quote: Eligible Countries Benin, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, Equatorial Guinea, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, Sao Tome and Principe, Sierra Leone, Togo

access.quote: are inviting proposals in the form of letters of inquiry (LOIs) for small grants

amount.quote: Grant Size: Large grants (US$50,000 to US$250,000)

reporting.quote: Recipients of large grants must submit financial reports each quarter and progress reports every six months through ConservationGrants.

effort.quote: Large-grant applicants submit letters of inquiry online, through the online grants database ConservationGrants. Small-grant applicants submit letters of inquiry using an offline template that will be provided in the open call instructions.

These applicants will have a defined period of time (typically around two months, although this may vary among hotspots) to submit a complete project proposal through the online portal ConservationGrants.
If a project triggers one or more safeguard policies, the grantee will be asked to prepare the relevant safeguard document(s) and incorporate related measures into the project's design.

eligibility.quote: The project must also support at least one strategic direction outlined in the CEPF ecosystem profile for the hotspot.
Organizations must have their own bank account and be authorized under relevant national laws to receive charitable contributions.

If you represent a government-owned enterprise or institution, you are eligible only if you can establish that the enterprise or institution: Has a legal personality independent of any government agency or actor Has the authority to apply for and receive private funds May not assert a claim of sovereign immunity

CEPF does not fund the following activities: Use of child labor or forced labor. Construction or rehabilitation of large or complex dams. Payment of salaries or salary supplements to government security personnel. Purchase of firearms or other weapons.
Les projets du CEPF ne doivent pas impliquer la réinstallation physique de personnes (qu'elle soit volontaire ou involontaire) ou l'achat de terres.
Activities that introduce or use potentially invasive, non-indigenous species.
Removal or alteration of any tangible cultural heritage.

Les projets du CEPF ne doivent pas causer d'impacts négatifs sur les habitats critiques, y compris de l'approvisionnement en ressources naturelles, à l'exception des impacts négatifs à une échelle limitée résultant d'actions de conservation qui permettent d'obtenir un gain net de valeurs de biodiversité.

after_award.quote: Large-grant recipients are required to attend a CEPF online orientation training within the first three months of their project's start date.
Recipients of large grants must submit financial reports each quarter and progress reports every six months through ConservationGrants.
